title: WSLua: Add capture file path function
description:
Add get_capture_file_path() so Lua scripts can get the current capture file path.

The function returns an absolute path when a capture file is open. It returns nil when no capture file path is available.

Add support in the applications that load WSLua and add a Lua test.

Closes #11316.

AI-Assisted: yes (ChatGPT)

notes.body: Why would this functionality need to be a "callback"?  Isn't this a simple "get" function?  I do like the suggestion in #11316 to just create a whole structure of "capture file information", not just the filename if we are going to add such a feature.

From Lua point of view it is just a get function. Lua code does not need to use any callbacks, it just calls get_capture_file_path() and gets the path.

The callback is only in C code because WSLua does not own the current capture_file. Each application has its own state, for example tshark has cfile and Qt uses CaptureFile::globalCapFile().

I don't think returning the whole capture_file to Lua is appropriate here. It is a large internal structure with many states, and I’m not sure that everything in it would actually be useful to expose to Lua code.

 #ifdef __cplusplus

+struct _capture_file;
+
+typedef struct _capture_file *(*wslua_capture_file_callback)(void);
+
+/**
+ * @brief Sets a callback used by Lua to get the current capture file.
+ *
+ * Applications embedding WSLua call this once at startup to provide a way
+ * to retrieve the currently active capture file. The callback returns NULL
+ * when no file is open.
+ *
+ * @param cb A callback returning a pointer to the current capture_file.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC void wslua_set_capture_file_callback(wslua_capture_file_callback cb);
+
+/**
+ * @brief Returns the current capture file, or NULL if none is open.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC struct _capture_file *wslua_get_capture_file(void);

+local testlib = require("testlib")
+local INIT = "init"
+local BASIC = "basic"
+local FMT = "format"
+
+testlib.init({ [INIT] = 1, [BASIC] = 7, [FMT] = 5 })
+
+local expect_type = "pcap"
+local expect_compression = "none"
+local expect_encap = "ether"
+
+for _, a in ipairs({...}) do
+    local k, v = a:match("^([^=]+)=(.*)$")
+    if k == "expect_type" then expect_type = v end
+    if k == "expect_compression" then expect_compression = v end
+    if k == "expect_encap" then expect_encap = v end
+end
+
+testlib.testing(INIT)
+testlib.test(INIT, "nil-before-open", get_capture_file_info() == nil)
+
+local tap = Listener.new()
+local checked = false
+
+function tap.packet()
+    if checked then return end
+    checked = true
+
+    local info = get_capture_file_info()
+
+    testlib.testing(BASIC)
+    testlib.test(BASIC, "table",         type(info) == "table")
+    testlib.test(BASIC, "path-string",   type(info.path) == "string")
+    testlib.test(BASIC, "path-absolute", info.path:sub(1,1) == "/" or info.path:match("^%a:[/\\]") ~= nil)
+    testlib.test(BASIC, "is-tempfile",   info.is_tempfile == false)
+    testlib.test(BASIC, "unsaved",       info.unsaved_changes == false)
+    testlib.test(BASIC, "size-positive", info.size > 0)
+    testlib.test(BASIC, "packets",       info.packet_count > 0)
+
+    testlib.testing(FMT)
+    testlib.test(FMT, "type",       info.type == expect_type)
+    testlib.test(FMT, "type-desc",  type(info.type_description) == "string")
+    testlib.test(FMT, "encap",      info.encap == expect_encap)
+    testlib.test(FMT, "encap-desc", type(info.encap_description) == "string")
+    testlib.test(FMT, "compression", info.compression == expect_compression)
+end
+
+function tap.draw()
+    testlib.getResults()
+end
